description: Composite group merging two captions: Fig. 9 (SEM + EDS) and Fig. 8 (four optical micrographs). Fig. 9(a) is a scanning electron micrograph of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–1.5Be strip rolled at 1050 °C showing the junction of austenite and ferrite: a dark, white-outlined elongated region boxed in red and labelled "A" (1 µm scale bar). Fig. 9(b)–(e) are EDS element-distribution maps of the same field, each with a 1 µm scale bar: (b) Fe (uniform magenta), (c) Mn (dark teal, red box A), (d) C (black with sparse cyan counts), (e) Al (olive-brown, red box A). Fig. 8 contains four optical micrographs (50 µm scale bars, RD arrow pointing up) of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe rolled at 1050 °C: (a) 0Be, (b) 0.5Be, (c) 1.0Be, (d) 1.5Be. (a) and (b) show γ-Fe matrix with dark needle-like compounds and red-circled/red-line-marked "Annealing twin"; (b) additionally labels blue-arrowed "Be-Fe phase" particles. (c) and (d) develop a strongly banded structure in which magenta arrows mark α-Fe bands, blue arrows "Be-Fe phase" and black arrows γ-Fe. The figure argues that increasing Be converts the single γ-Fe rolled structure into a banded α + γ dual-phase structure with dispersed Be–Fe phase.
measured_quantities: scale bar of Fig. 8 optical micrographs (µm) = 50
scale bar of Fig. 9 SEM image and EDS maps (µm) = 1

observations.observation: The four optical micrographs in Fig. 8 all carry a 50 µm scale bar and a vertical black RD (rolling direction) arrow at the lower left.
Fig. 8(a), the 0Be steel, shows a γ-Fe matrix containing dark needle-like compounds, with red circles and a red ellipse annotating features labelled 'Annealing twin'.

Fig. 8(b), the 0.5Be steel, shows a well-defined grain-boundary network and small dark particles that blue arrows label 'Be-Fe phase'; multiple red parallel-line marks labelled 'Annealing twin' are drawn.

In Fig. 8(c) (1.0Be) and Fig. 8(d) (1.5Be) the microstructure is banded, with magenta arrows labelled 'α-Fe', a blue arrow labelled 'Be-Fe phase', black arrows labelled 'γ-Fe' and a red ellipse labelled 'Annealing twin'.
The four rolled strips shown in the optical micrographs are 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C processed by rolling at 1050 °C.

The SEM panel (a) of Fig. 9 shows the junction of austenite and ferrite in Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–1.5Be strip rolled at 1050 °C, and panels (b)–(e) are the element distributions of Fe, Mn, C and Al respectively.
In the EDS maps the Fe map is uniformly bright magenta, whereas the C map is almost black with only sparse high-intensity dots, indicating very few detectable carbon X-rays in this field.
The red rectangle 'A' drawn on the SEM image (Fig. 9a) is repeated at the same position in the Mn map (c) and the Al map (e), marking the region analysed for elemental contrast.
Both the SEM image and every EDS map carry a 1 µm scale bar.
The needle-like compounds produced by beryllium addition in the as-cast microstructure still exist after thermal deformation and heat treatment, but their distribution trend and size were changed.
Annealing twins are observed in the rolled microstructure.
With increasing beryllium addition the amount of precipitated beryllium compounds increases and their distribution becomes more dispersed.
In the fully austenitic steels (0Be and 0.5Be) the grain size increases after the addition of beryllium.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of the 0Be Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C strip rolled at 1050 °C; matrix labelled γ-Fe with dark needle-like/platelet precipitates aligned along deformation bands, faint needle structure across the field. Two red circles and a red ellipse mark features labelled 'Annealing twin'. RD arrow at lower left, 50 µm scale bar at lower right.

Optical micrograph of the 0.5Be strip: clearly delineated dark grain-boundary network in the γ-Fe matrix with dark needle-like precipitates inside grains and along boundaries. Several red parallel-line marks and ellipses are labelled 'Annealing twin'; pairs of blue arrows point to small dark particles labelled 'Be-Fe phase'. RD arrow and 50 µm scale bar.

Optical micrograph of the 1.0Be strip: a wavy, banded two-phase structure. Magenta arrows label lighter bands 'α-Fe', a blue arrow labels dark particle-decorated bands 'Be-Fe phase', black arrows label 'γ-Fe', and red ellipses mark 'Annealing twin'. RD arrow and 50 µm scale bar.

Optical micrograph of the 1.5Be strip: strongly elongated, vertically banded structure with long light bands labelled 'α-Fe' (magenta arrows), dark particle-rich bands labelled 'Be-Fe phase' (blue arrow), black-arrowed 'γ-Fe', and a red ellipse labelled 'Annealing twin'. RD arrow and 50 µm scale bar.

SEM micrograph of Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–1.5Be rolled at 1050 °C showing the junction of austenite and ferrite: dark blocky/elongated phase regions outlined in white inside a lighter matrix, with a red rectangle labelled 'A' drawn over the central junction. 1 µm scale bar (caption states this is the austenite/ferrite junction).
EDS map of Fe (top-right label 'Fe'): uniformly high magenta/purple signal over the whole field with dark spots at the positions of the second-phase particles. 1 µm scale bar.

EDS map of Mn (top-right label 'Mn'): dark teal field with the same red rectangle 'A' as in (a); the boxed junction region A appears as a visible contrast feature relative to the surrounding matrix. 1 µm scale bar.
EDS map of C (top-right label 'C'): nearly black field with only sparse cyan/blue speckles, i.e. very low carbon X-ray counts across the mapped area. 1 µm scale bar.
EDS map of Al (top-right label 'Al'): olive/brown-yellow field with dark particle positions and the red rectangle 'A' in the upper-left, matching the region boxed in (a) and (c). 1 µm scale bar.

unreadable_items: Fig. 9(a): individual fine particles inside the boxed region A are not resolvable and carry no printed phase labels
Fig. 9(c) and (e): whether the boxed region A is enriched or depleted in Mn and Al cannot be quantified because no colour scale or intensity legend is printed on the maps
No numeric composition or grain-size values are printed on any panel
